newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger after volatile session.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger after volatile session.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Thursday, underperforming their U.S. counterparts in a volatile session with the market looking ahead to the prospect of a Bank of Canada rate cut, analysts said.

"It was a very volatile day," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada. "The reason we underperformed the U.S. later in the day was because the U.S. did very well after the auction."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.30 to C$114.80 to yield 6.789 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 29/32 to yield 6.55 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 24 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading Wednesday.

Canadian bonds were pulled lower by U.S. Treasuries earlier in the session after a Japanese finance ministry official was quoted saying the U.S. dollar's recent recovery will end soon. The report prompted a selloff in the U.S. dollar and sparked concern that investment flows from Japan into the Canadian bond market could dry up.
"The threat that (Japanese flows) might be stopped with a potentially stronger yen started us off on a negative tone," said Chandler.
Canadian bonds then rebounded with Treasuries after the successful U.S. auction of 30-year bonds.

Analysts said the Canadian market is now awaiting a rate cut by the Bank of Canada which could come as early as tomorrow. The Bank of Canada is expected to cut rates to offset the tightening impact on the economy of a stronger dollar.

"The currency is below C$1.3300 (US$0.7519) so there seems a very high probability that it (an ease) is going to occur to offset the currency move," said Dan Kelly, director of financial market research with CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc.
